extraction.name: FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark
extraction.description: An evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains. These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P.-J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., Krishnan, S., Ranzato, M., Guzmán, F., & Fan, A. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv:2106.03193v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia (specifically Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage) and translated into 101 languages by professional translators through Language Service Providers (LSPs).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentence selection involved selecting an article at random from each source, manually selecting contiguous sentences (3-5), avoiding short or malformed sentences, and balancing paragraph location (beginning, middle, end) to avoid document structure bias.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Professional translators translated sentences via LSPs. The workflow included: 1) Translation and editing by an LSP. 2) Automatic quality checks (language ID, copy checks, length, fluency, engine copy detection). 3) Human quality assurance by an independent LSP. Re-translation was required if the Translation Quality Score was below 90%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation Quality Score was calculated based on identified errors (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, register) and severity levels (minor, major, critical). Mistranslation was the largest error category observed.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 professional translation per item (with editing and QA)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Sentence selection annotators: 10 lab members (6 male, 4 female), roles included researchers and program/project managers, from regions including East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America. Translators: Professional translators (demographics not specified).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language identification, copy detection (source and translation engine), length checks, language model fluency checks, SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU) for similarity heuristics.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The test set is available via a publicly available evaluation server to prevent overfitting, while dev and devtest sets are publicly downloadable. There are plans to expand the number of languages covered.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Fosters progress in machine translation for low-resource languages; enables evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems; supports measurement of regionally-relevant language pairs (e.g., Spanish-Aymara, Vietnamese-Thai).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential translationese bias for non-English source sentences (human-translated); bias mitigation in sentence selection by balancing paragraph location; domain bias (WikiNews slightly easier, WikiVoyage harder due to named entities).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Translationese effects for non-English source sentences; test set not publicly released (only via server); performance heavily correlated with training data availability; WikiVoyage domain may be harder due to local named entities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of many-to-many multilingual machine translation; document-level translation; multimodal translation; text classification; language identification; multilingual domain adaptation.
